Q: Kind of issue with two-steps recursion A:

The answer by Thomas describes the problem very well, but it lacks a solution. The solution of course is to use the convoy pattern:

Definition nat_ind2 :=
  fun (P : nat -> Prop) (P0 : P 0) (P1 : P 1)
  (HypInd : (forall n : nat, P n -> P (S n) -> P (S (S n)))) =>
    fix f (n:nat) := match n as n2 return (P n2) with
                     | 0 => P0
                     | S n1 => match n1 as n2 return P n2 -> (P (S n2)) with
                       | 0 => fun _ => P1
                       | S n0 => fun Hn2 => HypInd n0 (f n0) Hn2
                    end (f n1) end.

Q: Which is more suitable in production environment, python zip vs enumerate? A:

Both things are built-in Python functions and are "suitable for production" - but this pattern is an obvious use case for enumerate - by doing the zip(range(len(a)), a) you are basically re-inventing the enumerate wheel, when there is absolutely no need for that.

As a rule of thumb, assume that if you are doing range(len(sequence)) in Python you are mostly using "foreign language accent".

Internally, that is even worse: by writing the expression yourself you are creating a new iterator where there was just one - that ordinarily won't give you a noticeable difference in performance, but it is far less elegant. (The Python VM will still have to deal with two iterators internally, and create a tuple with (index, item) for each item - so code-amount-wise per cycle the work is the same - but enumerate can have specific optimizations now or in the future that wouldn't apply to the zip form)

Q: Diagnosing and Addressing MongoDB Connection Error in Server Configuration A:

I had the same problem in a Caddy server setup.

It turned out to be the rate limiting of Letsencrypt: if you debug a server setup you might accidentially ask for too many certificates from Letsencrypt. It then lets you wait a few hours before you get another one.

To see if that is the problem simply wait a few hours and try again.

Q: How do I await in Javascript jupyter? A:

I'm guessing it depends on the kernel used (ijavascript which I initially installed does not support it), but this kernel ijavascript-await (from the same developer) supports await in the cells.

It does not do it exactly as I'd expect it like:

[5]: await Promise.resolve(123);

[5]: 123

Instead it prints:

[5]: await Promise.resolve(123);

[5]: Promise { <pending> }

but at least it otherwise works correctly. That is, you'd get:

[5]: a = await Promise.resolve(123)
     a += 2

[5]: Promise { <pending> }
____________________________________________________________________

[6]: a

[6]: 125

Q: Send file path as alias via Slack message A:

Looking at the client documentation, you probably need to pass your string using the markdown_text parameter, like so:

client.chat_postMessage(channel=channel, markdown_text=message)

Q: TailwindCSS for beginners A:

Learning vanilla CSS is invaluable as a beginner, because that's the foundation on which frameworks (like Tailwind) are built. I suggest sticking to plain CSS for a while, then switching to Tailwind once you're comfortable. This will also give you the flexibility to work with other frameworks because you'll have a more grounded understanding of CSS. Best of luck!

Q: How to sign ClickOnce manifest files (.application, .manifest) when using Google Cloud KMS for code signing? A:

I finally resolved this using Relic (a standalone signing tool by SAS) and Mage. The key is the specific order of operations:

  1. Use mage -update on the .manifest.

  2. Sign the .manifest with Relic (which supports GCP KMS natively).

  3. Use mage -update -AppManifest on the .application file to link the newly signed manifest.

  4. Finally, sign the .application and .exe files with Relic.

This 'Sign -> Update -> Sign' sequence prevents the HashValidation and IdentityMismatch errors common when switching to KMS-backed certificates.
